children: The Investment & Development Conversations session, titled ‘India Under Construction: Building the Next Hospitality Decade’, brought together developers, hotel companies and investment leaders to discuss the development pipeline and the forces shaping India’s next phase of hospitality expansion

The 10th edition of the prestigious BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026), hosted at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity, is bringing leading voices from across the hospitality industry for the next two days of conversations on the sector’s growth and evolution. With the theme
‘India’s Hospitality Decade: From Growth to Greatness’
, the Summit will examine the opportunities, challenges and shifts shaping India’s hospitality landscape as the industry enters a defining decade.
The Investment & Development Conversations session, titled
‘India Under Construction: Building the Next Hospitality Decade’
, brought together developers, hotel companies and investment leaders to discuss the development pipeline and the forces shaping India’s next phase of hospitality expansion.
Karan Mahesh, Regional Director, South & Southeast Asia, STR, Singapore

Rohit Dar, VP & Head of South Asia, Ascott International Management India; Sonica Malhotra Kandhari, Joint MD, MBD Group ; Manoj Agarwal, Chief Growth & Product Officer, Chalet Hotels; Souvagya Mohapatra, MD - India, Nepal, Bhutan & Sri Lanka, Atmosphere Core; and Sharad Bhargava, Head of Development, Eurasia, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts.

Dar said, “At the end of the day, you’re building a hotel to make money, and that’s the most important thing. To make that happen, you have to have the right fit between the brand and the market. Owners have aspirations, but the brand must be as honest as possible about what kind of branding will work.”

Kandhari addressed, “People who understand the Indian territory play an important role, because when you talk about residentials, you already have cash flows coming in. You always need a partner who understands both sides of the coin.”

Agarwal explained, “You have to look at all the possible options, because sometimes one asset class is complementary to the other. We look at all the different asset classes before finalising each component of any project, as one segment can complement the other and, when combined, provide the best-case return scenario.”

Mohapatra said, “Construction and execution are not major constraints, as India is already delivering large volumes of commercial and residential space every year. The biggest constraint over the next 10 years could be the quality of capital, with hospitality requiring patient capital that is commensurate with the industry’s long-term gestation. The sector remains fragmented, slow and complex, with approvals, environmental clearances and financing adding to the challenges of development.”

Bhargava addressed,“Life safety becomes a huge issue to solve when plans have been made, construction has started and staircases are already in place. Owners should first and most importantly finalise the brand they want to work with, whether it is economy, mid-scale or luxury, and should not start work until the brand is finalised.”

As the discussion drew to a close, speakers emphasised that the next decade of growth will not be defined by paper pipelines, but by built assets and delivered returns. By strengthening brand-owner alignment and focussing on high-potential destination creation, the industry can unlock the capital necessary to turn India's hospitality blueprint into reality.

The two-day BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) encompasses over 25 sessions where hospitality veterans and experts across the nation gathered to provide diverse knowledge and insights. The Summit & Awards is a testament to BW Hotelier’s commitment towards revolutionising Indian hospitality by honouring the crème de la crème of the industry.
